transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, well, it's... it's a lot, to be honest. What really made me come in today, like what finally pushed me to actually make the appointment, is everything going on at my job right now. I'm a buyer, I do wholesale and retail purchasing, so I'm dealing with a ton of inventory, forecasting, you know, setting up product launches and dealing with suppliers all day. It's a lot to keep track of. 

But recently, I just... I can't shake this feeling. Actually, it's more than a feeling, it's like this constant weight because I know that people at work, and even some of the external vendors we use, are tracking my buys. Like, they're secretly monitoring my purchase orders and then deliberately messing with the launch numbers behind my back just to make me look completely stupid. I know how crazy that might sound to someone on the outside, but it is happening. They're altering the data or the inventory counts to sabotage me. 

And it's just so incredibly frustrating because I tried to bring it up, I even sat down with my supervisor about it, and he pulled up all the system reports and the analytics to try and prove to me that the data doesn't show anyone tampering with anything. He spent like an hour going line by line, showing me that the reports don't prove it, but I just can't let it go because I know what I'm seeing. The numbers don't add up to what I originally put in, and it's like this whole coordinated thing between the office and the vendors to ruin my track record, and I just can't get anyone there to take it seriously... so, yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you think people are out to get you outside of work as well?

Well, outside of work... I mean, mostly it's work, but honestly, it bleeds into everything because my mind is just always on it. Like, I'll be at the grocery store, just trying to buy some cereal or whatever, and I'll see someone looking at their phone, and I immediately think, 'Are they connected to the suppliers? Are they texting someone about me right now?' But the core of it, the real issue that brought me in here, is definitely what's happening with my job. 

I just... I can't shake this feeling, you know? It's like this heavy, suffocating feeling that people at work, my colleagues, the inventory team, and even those external vendors we contract with, they are all actively tracking my buys. Every single purchase order I submit, every forecast I put together. And they aren't just watching; they are deliberately messing with the launch numbers. They're changing the quantities or the delivery dates just to make me look completely stupid in front of management. 

And the worst part is, like I said, I went to my supervisor. I sat in his office, and he pulled up the entire ERP system on his big monitor, and we went through the reports. He kept pointing to the screen, saying, 'Look, the logs don't show anyone else logging in, the timestamps match your entries, the reports don't prove that anyone is tampering with it.' He spent so much time trying to convince me it was in my head, just pointing at the data, but I know what I submitted. I know the numbers I typed in, and what's in the system now is not what I entered. So even when he shows me those reports and says they don't prove it, I just know they've found some way around the system logs. They're doing it, and it's all just to ruin me.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't think people were sabotaging you at work?

Well, yeah, I mean... it wasn't always like this. There was definitely a time when I didn't feel this way at all. When I first started out doing the wholesale buying, I actually really liked it. I felt like I had a good handle on the inventory and the forecasting, and I honestly trusted the people I worked with, you know? I thought we were all on the same team, working toward the same goals for the retail side. 

But... if I really sit down and look at the timeline, like really look at when things started going off the rails and getting weird, it's been roughly ten months now. Yeah, about ten months since all these suspicious beliefs really took hold and I first realized what they were doing to my purchase orders. I remember it was just a small discrepancy at first, but then it kept happening. And, um, it's actually not just the suspicions about the sabotage either, because right around that exact same time, about ten months ago, that's also when the voice started. Just... this voice that I hear, kind of chiming in and feeding into it all, telling me about what they're doing behind my back. 

So for almost a whole year now, well, ten months to be exact, it's just been this relentless cycle. Every single day I go into the office, and I have to deal with the sabotage, and the voice, and just trying to keep my head above water while they actively mess with my launch numbers. Before those ten months, I swear, everything was completely normal. I was just a regular guy doing my job. But since then, it's just... it's all I can focus on, and it takes up so much of my energy just trying to track what they're changing.
Can you describe what the voice sounds like?

Well, it's... it's definitely a man's voice. It's deep, kind of gruff, and it sounds incredibly real. Like, I'll be in the back, in the stockroom, which is usually pretty quiet because most of the inventory team is up front at their desks, and I'll just be trying to pull some samples or check a physical count against the system—because, like I said, I have to double-check absolutely everything now with all the tampering going on—and suddenly I'll hear it. Or another time it happens a lot is when I'm driving back from a vendor meeting. The drive from our main supplier takes about forty-five minutes, mostly highway, so I'm just in my car, windows rolled up, totally alone. 

But then, out of nowhere, it sounds like this man is literally right behind me. Right over my shoulder, so close I can almost feel someone there. And he'll just say, clear as day, 'Move faster, Scott.' Just like that. Or sometimes he doesn't even tell me what to do, he just... laughs. He'll start laughing at my picks, like he's mocking the inventory items I just selected for the purchase orders, just this totally condescending laugh right in my ear. 

And every single time it happens, my heart just drops and I whip around. I turn around so fast in the stockroom, or I'll check my rearview mirror and physically look into the backseat of my car, fully expecting to see some guy standing right there or hiding behind my seat. But... there's nobody. It's just me. Empty stockroom, empty car. And I just sit there trying to figure out how someone could have sneaked up on me, or if maybe it was a radio or a speaker, but there's never a radio. It's just so unsettling because I'm already so stressed about the numbers and the vendors, and then I have this guy literally breathing down my neck and laughing at me, and it just makes the whole thing so much harder to deal with when I'm just trying to do my job.
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that you feel you must do?

Well, no, not really like a command I have to follow, you know? It's not like he's saying, 'Go do this terrible thing right now or else.' It's more just... like I said, it's that gruff man's voice, and it happens when I'm alone in the stockroom or, you know, doing that long forty-five-minute drive back from a vendor meeting. He'll just be right there, practically breathing on my neck, and he says, 'Move faster, Scott.' 

And it's not that I feel like I *must* do it, it's more like it just startles the living daylights out of me. Because I'll be in my own head, stressing about the purchase orders and the launch numbers, and then suddenly there's this guy telling me to hurry up, or worse, he's just laughing at the inventory picks I just made. Just this deep, mocking laugh. And my immediate reaction is always just pure panic, like, 'Who is in here with me?' I whip around so fast, I mean, I've almost pulled a muscle in my neck turning around in the car, fully expecting to see some guy sitting in the backseat, or standing right behind me in the aisle of the stockroom. But then... there's just nobody. It's completely empty. So I don't feel compelled to obey him, it's just... it's incredibly distracting and terrifying when you're just trying to do your job and you think someone is literally right there mocking you.
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that you feel you cannot ignore?

Well, like I was just saying, it's not really about whether I can ignore it or not, it's more about how impossible it is to ignore someone when they sound like they're standing right on top of you. I mean, think about it. If you were just sitting there, totally alone, maybe in your car on a long stretch of highway—like when I do that drive back from the main supplier, which is a solid forty-five minutes of just me and the road—and suddenly, out of nowhere, you hear this deep, gruff man's voice right over your shoulder. Right there. And he says, 'Move faster, Scott.' 

You can't just ignore that. It's not like a passing thought or a song stuck in your head. It's a physical reaction. My heart jumps into my throat, my hands grip the steering wheel, and I whip my head around so fast to check the backseat because my brain is telling me, 'There is a man in this car with you.' And the same thing happens at work. I'll be back in the stockroom, which is usually dead quiet because everyone else is up front, and I'm just trying to pull samples or check the physical count against the system, and suddenly he's there. Just... laughing. This mocking, condescending laugh right in my ear, like he thinks the inventory items I picked are just a joke. 

So, it's not that I feel like I *have* to do what he says, or that I can't ignore a command. It's that you physically cannot ignore the sound of another human being standing inches away from you when you know for a fact you're supposed to be alone. I turn around every single time. Every time. I look behind me in the stockroom, I check the rearview mirror, I look over my shoulder in the car, and every time... there's just nobody there. It's just empty air. But in that split second when I hear him, ignoring him isn't even an option because it's just so incredibly real and startling.
Do you ever have days where you don't think people are sabotaging you at work?

Well, you'd think so, right? Like, if things just settled down in my head, maybe that would stop too. But... no, not really. Because there was this one stretch, maybe a little while back, where things actually did get pretty quiet for me. I was finally sleeping normally again, which was huge. I was actually getting a solid seven or eight hours a night instead of just running on fumes and espresso shots. And I didn't have that... that intense, buzzing energy anymore. For a while before that, I honestly felt like I was single-handedly running the whole market, like I was the only wholesale buyer in the entire region who knew what they were doing and I was going to revolutionize the whole supply chain. 

But that feeling faded. I leveled out. I was just going to work, coming home, eating dinner, sleeping totally fine. It was a really calm stretch. But the thing is, even during that calmer stretch—and this lasted for a good few weeks—I still absolutely knew they were messing with me. I still spent those entire few weeks believing people were tracking my buys. I would sit there at my desk, feeling completely physically rested, not hyped up at all, but I'd look at the purchase orders and I just knew someone was monitoring my keystrokes or altering the vendor codes to mess up my inventory counts. 

And the voice didn't stop either. I'd be back in the stockroom, totally calm, just doing a routine physical count, and I'd still hear him. That same gruff guy, right over my shoulder, even though I was sleeping great and completely level-headed about my job. So, even when everything else was fine and I wasn't feeling like some untouchable market genius, the tracking and the voice in the stockroom were still there for weeks on end. It just... it never really stops, no matter how calm I am.
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that would harm yourself or others?

No, no, never anything like that. It's never violent or... or telling me to hurt anyone, or myself, thank God. It's just... well, like I was telling you before, it's just really intrusive and annoying, and mostly just startling. It's always that same gruff voice, and it's always in those specific situations, you know? Like when I'm alone in the stockroom, trying to focus on the inventory counts, or when I'm on that long drive back from a vendor meeting. It's never, 'Hey, go drive your car into a ditch,' or 'Go punch your manager.' It's just... he's just there, right behind me. 

Like I said, he'll just say, 'Move faster, Scott.' Or he'll just do that deep, mocking laugh when I'm pulling items for an order, like he thinks my picks are completely wrong or stupid. And it's so clear, it sounds exactly like a real person is standing right over my shoulder, breathing down my neck. It's so real that I always, always turn around. I whip my head around to look behind me in the stockroom, or I check the backseat of my car, fully expecting to see some guy standing there judging me. But then, of course, there's nobody there. It's just me. So, no, he doesn't tell me to do anything dangerous or harmful, it's just this constant, startling presence telling me to hurry up or laughing at my work when I'm supposed to be completely alone.
Do you ever think people are out to get you or sabotaging you when you're not thinking about work?

Well, I mean, it's mostly centered around work, because that's where the stakes are, you know? But it bleeds over, it definitely bleeds over into my off-hours because I just can't turn it off. I'll be at home, sitting on the couch, trying to watch TV or just eat dinner, and my mind is just racing, going over every single purchase order, every vendor interaction. And that's actually the main reason I finally decided to come in and talk to someone. It's just exhausting. Because I know, I absolutely know, that people at work—and even some of the outside vendors, which is the craziest part because they're supposed to be our partners—I know they are actively tracking my buys. 

They're monitoring what I do, and I'm convinced they are deliberately messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. Like, they want me to fail. I'll be sitting at home on a Saturday, completely off the clock, and I'll just be obsessing over how they probably went into the system and altered the quantities I ordered for a new product rollout. And the thing is, I've even brought this up. I went to my supervisor, and I laid it all out for him, and he actually sat down and pulled the reports right in front of me. He showed me the logs, the keystrokes, the final numbers, and he kept saying, "Look, Scott, nobody is changing your numbers. The reports don't show any tampering." 

But even when I'm looking right at the screen, right at the data he's pointing to, I just can't shake the feeling. I walk away from his desk and I think, "Well, they're just covering their tracks really well, or maybe the system itself is compromised." So even when I'm not at the office, even when I'm supposed to be relaxing, I'm just consumed by this certainty that there's this whole coordinated effort to sabotage my numbers and ruin my reputation with the higher-ups. It just never leaves my head, no matter where I am or what time of day it is.
How long have you been hearing the voice?

Well, if I really sit down and try to map out the exact timeline... you know, tracing it all back to when I first started noticing that gruff guy in the stockroom, and when I first realized my purchase orders were being messed with... it’s been a pretty long stretch. I’d say it’s been roughly ten months now. Yeah, about ten months for both the voice and the whole situation with my numbers. 

I remember because it was right around the time we were getting this massive influx of new vendor catalogs last year, and I was spending hours upon hours in the back, just going over the physical inventory counts. That’s when I first heard him. At first, I tried to brush it off, thinking, well, maybe the warehouse just echoes weirdly, or maybe it’s just the hum from the big HVAC units playing tricks on my ears when I'm stressed out. But then it just kept happening, and right around that exact same time, I started noticing the discrepancies in my launch numbers and realized they were tracking my buys. 

So for ten solid months, day in and day out, it's just been this constant reality for me. Ten months of whipping my head around in the stockroom expecting to see someone standing there judging me, and ten months of having to double and triple-check my logs because I know they're actively trying to sabotage my reputation with the higher-ups. It’s just... it's a really long time to carry all that, you know? You’d think after nearly a year of this you might get used to it, or it would just fade into the background, but it doesn't at all. It still startles me every single time I hear him, and the tracking still completely consumes my thoughts even when I'm just trying to sit on my couch and eat dinner.
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that you feel you must do, even if you don't want to?

No, no, it's never like a command where I feel like I have no choice, or like I'm being controlled like a puppet or something. It's not a... it doesn't force me to act. It's more just like having a really obnoxious, critical supervisor hovering right over my shoulder. Like I was saying before, it's always in those same situations. I'll be back in the stockroom, surrounded by boxes, just trying to get through my physical inventory counts, and it's so quiet back there, and then suddenly, right behind my right ear, I hear this gruff man's voice. He just says things like, "Move faster, Scott." Or I'll be picking items for a new order, trying to make sure the quantities are right before the system gets messed with, and he'll just let out this deep, mocking laugh. Like he's watching me and thinks my choices are completely idiotic. 

And it happens when I'm driving, too. I'll be on the highway, coming back from a vendor meeting, just staring at the road, and the exact same voice will speak up from the backseat. "Move faster, Scott." It's so incredibly clear. It's not a thought in my head, it sounds exactly like there is a physical human being standing right behind me in the stockroom or sitting right behind me in my car. I swear to you, I can almost feel the breath on my neck. It's so real that I physically react every single time. I whip my head around, my heart starts pounding, I drop my clipboard or I check my rearview mirror in a panic, fully expecting to see this guy standing there. I brace myself for the confrontation. But every time I turn around... there's absolutely nobody there. It's just empty space. So, he doesn't make me do things I don't want to do, he just... he just startles me and makes me feel like I'm constantly being judged and rushed when I'm supposed to be alone.
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that you feel compelled to do?

Well, like I think I just mentioned a second ago, no, it's really not like that at all. I don't feel compelled, you know, like I'm under some kind of spell or being forced against my will to do anything. It's exactly like I was just saying—it's just this gruff man's voice, and it happens specifically when I'm in the stockroom doing my inventory, or when I'm driving back from a vendor meeting. 

I'll be in the car, hands on the wheel, or I'll be in the back pulling items, and he just speaks up right behind my ear. He says, "Move faster, Scott," or he just lets out this awful, deep laugh right when I'm making my picks for the new orders. And even though I don't feel *compelled* to obey him like a robot, it does make me rush my work because it startles the absolute hell out of me. I mean, wouldn't you rush if someone was breathing down your neck? I literally spin around—whether I'm dropping my clipboard in the aisles or checking my rearview mirror on the highway—fully expecting to see this guy standing right there, invading my personal space. But every single time I turn around, nobody's there. It's just empty. So, no, it's not a compulsion to act, it's just... it's just him being there, criticizing me, laughing at my picks, and making me jump out of my skin when I'm completely alone.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your supervisor was telling the truth when he showed you the reports, and that there might not be anyone sabotaging you at work?

I mean... I’ve tried. I really have tried to just sit there in his office, look at the printouts he slides across the desk, and just accept them at face value. I’ll look at the spreadsheets, the launch numbers, the inventory logs, and I’ll tell myself, "Okay, Scott, maybe it’s just a clerical error, maybe the system glitched, maybe you just miscalculated the buy." But... I just can't. I can't shake the feeling. It’s like this heavy, sinking weight in my gut that tells me something else is going on. 

Because when I look at those reports, they just don't match what I know I did. I know what I ordered. I know the quantities I picked. I spend hours in that stockroom double-checking everything. And then suddenly the numbers are off? It just doesn’t make sense unless someone is actively messing with it. And it’s not just the people at work, either. I’ve started noticing weird things with some of the vendors, too. Like, the way they look at me during meetings, or the way they phrase things in emails... it feels like they’re all in on it. Like they’re all tracking my buys, coordinating with each other, and deliberately altering the launch numbers just to make me look completely incompetent. 

And my supervisor, he just points at the paper and says, "Look, the reports don't show any tampering." But of course they don't! If you were going to sabotage someone, you wouldn't leave a trail on the official reports, would you? You'd cover your tracks. So, yeah, he shows me the reports, and I try to believe him, I really do, but... the feeling just won't go away. It’s actually what really made me come in to see you, to be honest. This constant, nagging certainty that they are all tracking me and trying to make me look stupid... it’s exhausting. I just can't let it go, no matter how many spreadsheets he puts in front of me.
Have your beliefs about people sabotaging you at work ever changed or wavered over the past ten months?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I guess I have moments where I try to convince myself it’s all in my head, like I was just saying about sitting in his office and looking at the reports. I try to make myself believe that the numbers are just numbers and nobody is out to get me. But... no, it never really goes away. It hasn't wavered. It's just this constant, heavy feeling that I can't shake. 

It’s actually the main reason I finally decided to come in and see you, because it’s been going on for so long and it’s just so exhausting. I can't shake the feeling that people at work, and like I said, even some of the vendors we deal with, are actively tracking my buys. I know they are. I can feel it. They’re tracking what I do, and they’re deliberately messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. They want me to look incompetent. And it doesn't matter how many times my supervisor pulls me into his office and shows me those printed reports and says, "Look, Scott, there's no proof of this." Of course the reports don't prove it! They're not going to leave a paper trail if they're trying to sabotage me, right? They're smarter than that. They know how to manipulate the system so it looks like it's my fault. So, yeah, even when he shows me the spreadsheets and tries to tell me I'm wrong, my belief hasn't changed. If anything, it just makes me feel more isolated, because I know what's happening, and nobody else will admit it. It's just been this relentless certainty for the whole ten months, every single day I walk into that building or get on a call with a vendor. I just know they're doing it.
Have you ever had a moment where you doubted that people were sabotaging you at work?

I know I just said I try to make myself believe it, but... doubt? Real doubt? No, not really. I mean, I guess I have these fleeting seconds where I think, 'Scott, are you losing your mind? Is this all just a huge misunderstanding?' Like when my supervisor, Dave, pulls me into his office and he has that whole stack of printouts, right? He spreads them all out on his desk, pointing at the inventory logs and the launch numbers, and he gives me this look like he genuinely feels sorry for me. For a split second, I look at his face and I think, 'Okay, maybe he’s right. Maybe it’s just a glitch in the software.' We just updated our inventory management system back in January, so glitches happen, right? 

But then... then I look closer at the numbers. And that heavy feeling just rushes right back in. Because I know exactly what I ordered. I’m a buyer, I live and breathe these spreadsheets. I know what quantities I picked, I know the vendors I spoke to. And there is just no way, absolutely no way, that the numbers could be this off by accident. It’s what really made me come in to see you, honestly. It’s this inescapable reality that I can't shake. I know—I just *know*—that people at work, and even some of the vendors we deal with on a daily basis, are actively tracking my buys. They are monitoring everything I do, and they are intentionally messing with the launch numbers just to make me look incredibly stupid and incompetent. 

And Dave can show me all the reports he wants. He can highlight every single column and say, 'Look, there’s no proof, there’s no unauthorized access logged in the system.' But of course there isn't! If you're going to sabotage someone, you don't use your own login credentials, do you? You don't leave a paper trail. You manipulate things behind the scenes. So, no, I don't really doubt it. The reports don't prove anything except that whoever is doing this is smart enough to cover their tracks. It’s exhausting, just constantly knowing they’re doing this and having everyone act like I’m the one who’s crazy.
Have you ever had a moment where you genuinely believed that no one was sabotaging you at work?

I feel like we keep circling back to this, Doc, but... no. Genuinely believed it? Like, deep down in my core, actually thought everything was totally fine and normal? Never. Not once. 

Because you have to understand how my day actually works. I get in early, usually around 7 AM, I boot up the system, and I start pulling the overnight vendor logs. I'm looking at data from suppliers in three different time zones, right? I started doing this right out of high school, worked my way up to being a buyer, and I know my job inside and out. I know how these systems operate. So when you ask if I genuinely think no one is doing anything... I just can't get there. 

Honestly, that is exactly what really made me come in to see you in the first place. I just absolutely cannot shake the feeling that people at work, and even some of these external vendors we use, are actively tracking my buys. It’s like they have a magnifying glass on every single purchase order I generate, and they are deliberately messing with the launch numbers. And they're doing it specifically to make me look stupid. To make me look like I have no idea what I'm doing. 

And Dave, my supervisor, he means well, I guess. He’ll sit there with his coffee mug—the one with the stupid golf joke on it—and he’ll point at the printed reports and say, "Scott, the reports don't prove that anyone is doing this." But I keep telling him, and I guess I keep trying to explain it to you, too... of course they don't! If I was going to sabotage a buyer, I wouldn't leave a giant red flag in the system logs for Dave to find. I'd do it quietly. I'd manipulate the back-end data so the reports look clean. So, no, even when he shows me those reports and tells me they don't prove anything, it doesn't change my mind for a second. I’ve never genuinely believed I’m just making this up. It's just this constant, heavy reality every single day, and I just... I can't shake it. It's why I'm sitting here in this chair right now, because I don't know how much longer I can deal with them doing this to me.

I feel like you're asking the exact same question just worded slightly differently, Doc. And I don't mean to be difficult, I really don't, but my answer is still exactly the same. No. Not even for a short time. Not for a minute, not for a second. 

It’s like... imagine if you knew, for a fact, that the sky was blue, and someone kept asking you, 'But did you ever think it was green, just for a little bit?' You wouldn't, right? Because you can see it. That’s how this is for me. And like I keep trying to explain, what really made me come in here to see you, what finally pushed me to make this appointment and sit in this room, is that I just can't shake the feeling that people at work and even some of those vendors are tracking my buys. It’s a constant weight. I can literally feel them monitoring my screen, tracking my keystrokes, watching every purchase order I submit. 

And they are deliberately messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. They want me out. They want me to look like this uneducated kid who got in over his head right out of high school. And it is so incredibly frustrating, because I know I do good work, but they manipulate the data so it looks like I completely botched the inventory. And I have to sit there, week after week, even when my supervisor shows me the reports don't prove that. Dave just taps his pen on the paper and says, 'Scott, look at the data, the data doesn't show anyone else logging in.' But I've said it a hundred times—of course the reports don't prove it! If you're going to alter launch numbers, you cover your tracks. You don't leave a neon sign pointing to your IP address. 

So, no. My belief hasn't changed. Not even for a fraction of a second. I just want it to stop, because I can't keep going into that office every day knowing they're doing this to me and having everyone, even Dave, act like I'm the one who's seeing things that aren't there.
Do you think people are out to get you in other areas of your life, outside of work?

Outside of work? Like, in my personal life? Well... no, not really. I mean, I don't really have a massive social life right now anyway, to be completely honest. I get off work, I drive back to my apartment—it's just this little one-bedroom over on the east side—and I try to just unwind. I'll watch some YouTube, maybe play some Xbox, try to do whatever a normal twenty-two-year-old is supposed to be doing. And when I'm doing that, I don't feel like my neighbors are listening through the walls, or like the guy delivering my pizza is trying to poison me, or anything crazy like that. I don't think the guys I play games with online are plotting against me. 

But... the problem is, my brain just doesn't shut off when I leave the office. Work kind of *is* my life, especially since I started there right out of high school and had to grind so hard just to get this buyer position. 

So even though I don't think random people on the street are out to get me, I'll be lying in bed at 2 AM, staring at the ceiling, and I'm right back in those spreadsheets. I know I keep sounding like a broken record, Doc, and I know you're trying to see if this is happening everywhere in my life, but I have to be clear... what really made me come in here, the entire reason I even picked up the phone to make this appointment, is that I just can't shake the feeling that people at work and even some of those vendors are tracking my buys. It’s just them. It's contained to that, but it's consuming me. I just obsess over how they are deliberately messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. 

And it just eats away at me because I can't prove it to anyone else. Like I keep saying, even when my supervisor shows me the reports and tells me they don't prove that anyone is doing it, the feeling doesn't go away. I know it's happening. So, no, it's not everyone everywhere. It's not my family or my neighbors. It's just the people connected to my job. But honestly? That's more than enough. It's ruining my life just from that.
